fichas.title: Direct, symmetrical lighting
fichas.summary: Direct symmetrical lighting is recommended for general lighting in workrooms, meeting rooms, public-access rooms and traffic zones. The page gives guidance on fitting shading angles and the assumed radiation angle for system design.
fichas.building_type: Workrooms, meeting rooms, public-access rooms and traffic zones

fichas.title: Wallwashers
fichas.summary: The page describes wallwashing arrangements for uniform wall illumination, including ceiling-grid or downlight wallwashers, rail-mounted wallwashers that also light part of the room, and ceiling-installed wallwashers that illuminate only the wall. Rail-mounted types are also described for display lighting in exhibitions and museums.

fichas.title: Directional spotlights and narrow-beam lighting
fichas.summary: Ceiling-mounted directional spotlights can create spatially differentiated lighting; their reflectors can be aimed vertically and horizontally. Narrow-beam rail lights offer selected beam angles, and their cones and spectra can be modified with lenses and filters. Glare protection is provided by louvres or anti-glare flaps.

fichas.title: Indirect and direct/indirect lighting
fichas.summary: Indirect lighting can create a bright room impression with low lighting levels and without reflected glare, but requires sufficient room height and careful coordination with the ceiling architecture. The page sets a ceiling-luminance limit for workplace lighting and notes higher energy consumption than direct lighting. Direct/indirect lighting is preferred when ceiling height is sufficient; the stated light distribution is 70% direct and 30% indirect.

fichas.title: Ceiling uplighters, floor downlighters and wall lights
fichas.summary: Ceiling uplighters and floor downlighters provide area lighting for ceilings or floors. Wall lights are used predominantly for decorative wall lighting and light effects, with limited illumination of the ceiling and floor.
uses: Area lighting of ceilings or floors
